They report a RISK DIFFERENCE in percentage points and this object pools a RISK RATIO; theirs is micro-ITT and this object's registered outcome text names no analysis population. Their interval excludes zero and this one includes one, and those are not contradictory statements about one quantity.

Abstract

Question. In adults with uncomplicated urinary tract infection, does gepotidacin differ from nitrofurantoin in therapeutic response (combined clinical and microbiological success) at the test-of-cure visit?1

Methods. estimates were pooled under a random-effects with the REML estimator; risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials); and certainty was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons.2

Results. Therapeutic response (combined clinical and microbiological), test-of-cure: risk ratio 1.2 (0.967 to 1.49) across 2 trials; 1 of these pooled outcome(s) carries a stated qualification -- a referral or a recorded finding -- given in full in Results and not reproduced here; the trials agreed loosely (I-squared 70.5%); and certainty of the evidence was very low.3

Refused: the Background sentence of the abstract. Background is argument -- why this question matters -- and no arrangement of the quantities this object holds yields it. It is emitted only from an authored field and there is no composition path for it here4
Refused: the Conclusions sentence of the abstract. A conclusion is argument -- what a reader should now believe -- and it is emitted only from an authored field. Composing one from the estimate would be this renderer telling the reader what to conclude, which no field supports5

Introduction

1Background. This review asks: In adults with uncomplicated urinary tract infection, does gepotidacin differ from nitrofurantoin in therapeutic response (combined clinical and microbiological success) at the test-of-cure visit? It pools 2 randomised trials, against nitrofurantoin. The outcome pooled is Therapeutic response (combined clinical and microbiological), test-of-cure. Every count and denominator behind those estimates is read as follows. Registry throughout. Every count and denominator in this pool is read from ClinicalTrials.gov posted results. No publication figure is used and no value is imported.

[Draft] The evidence identified on this question is 2 randomised trials (NCT04020341, NCT04187144), pooled here at 1.201 (95% CI 0.967 to 1.491) for therapeutic response (combined clinical and microbiological), test-of-cure visit. Certainty in that estimate is rated VERY_LOW, rated down for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness and imprecision. What this estimate does not establish is recorded in full with the result in Results, and is not restated here. Which of those unresolved points makes the question worth asking now is the author's judgement.2

[Draft] A search for published syntheses matched 25 record(s); 25 were read and 1 appraised against this review. The appraised synthesis is Subgroup Analysis of Pooled Phase 3 Efficacy Data from Two Randomized Trials of Gepotidacin Versus Nitrofurantoin in Uncomplicated Urinary Tract Infections (Clinical Infectious Diseases, 2026). Whether those differences warrant a new synthesis rather than citing the existing one is the author's judgement.3

Methods — synthesis

For therapeutic response (combined clinical and microbiological), test-of-cure, a random-effects model was fitted with the REML estimator.1

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials) (), following . 2 result-level assessments were made.2

A ceiling applies to every risk-of-bias judgement in this review; it is stated with the assessment itself rather than summarised here.3

Certainty of evidence was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons., following . 0 pooled outcome(s) were rated. No domain is rated UP. Rating up for a large effect, a dose-response gradient or opposing plausible confounding applies to observational evidence; these are randomised trials, which start HIGH and can only be rated down. 1 outcome(s) were not rated because their pool is declined or withdrawn: there is no effect estimate to rate the certainty of, and rating one would be certainty about a number this review refused to publish.4

Refused: the claim that records were screened in duplicate by two independent reviewers5

Results

The pooled risk ratio for therapeutic response (combined clinical and microbiological), test-of-cure was 1.2 (0.967 to 1.49) across 2 trials, against nitrofurantoin.1

Noted on this pool. Checked and clean. Read from the registrations on 2026-08-21: NCT04020341 registers 'Number of Participants With Therapeutic Response (Combined Per Participant Clinical and Microbiological Respon' (population: TR); NCT04187144 registers 'Number of Participants With Therapeutic Response (Combined Per Participant Clinical and Microbiological Respon' (population: TR). Both trials register the same primary in the same population, so this pool does not cross an analysis-population boundary. Recorded because a check that only speaks when it finds something cannot be told from a check that was never run. The sponsor's own pooled analysis of these exact two trials splits by nitrofurantoin susceptibility, and the effect is more than twice as large in the not-susceptible stratum: therapeutic success difference +9.6% [4.1, 15.2] where the uropathogen is susceptible against +20.8% [9.2, 32.4] where it is not (PMID 42413960, Clin Infect Dis 2026, EAGLE-2 NCT04020341 and EAGLE-3 NCT04187144). This pool collapses that split, so its single ratio is an average over two populations the published analysis keeps apart. They report a risk difference in percentage points and this object pools a risk ratio; theirs is micro-ITT and this object's registered outcome text names no analysis population. Their interval excludes zero and this one includes one, and those are not contradictory statements about one quantity. Whether these are non-inferiority designs is not established: the registration fields fetched do not use the word, and a pooled ratio from non-inferiority trials answers a different question from a superiority pool. Unresolved, not assumed. The pooled analysis is by the sponsor's investigators. That does not make it wrong and it is the most direct evidence about these two trials, but it is stated rather than treated as an independent referee.2

The trials' results were loosely consistent with one another: I-squared, the share of the variation between them that is more than chance alone would produce, was 70.5%; the estimated variance of the true effects between trials (tau-squared) was 0.0172, the heterogeneity test statistic Q was 3.39, on degrees of freedom 1.3

What this does not establish: Not that either trial is free of bias -- no risk-of-bias assessment is recorded, and a pooled estimate without one is an arithmetic result, not a graded finding. Not non-inferiority or superiority: both trials were designed as non-inferiority studies against an active comparator, and a risk ratio near 1 with an interval spanning 1 is the expected result of a successful non-inferiority trial rather than evidence of no difference. Not that the pooled interval is reliable at k=2 -- see the Hartung-Knapp interval, which is the honest width. Not agreement with any published synthesis; none has been checked.4

The full model output for every pooled outcome -- the call, the estimator, the heterogeneity statistics and the back-transformed interval -- is reproduced verbatim as Extended data at the end of this article, so every number above can be checked against the software that produced it.5

Risk of bias in the included results

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials). The unit of assessment is a result1

A domain that cannot be judged from the sources read is NO_INFORMATION, never LOW. Low-by-default asserts a fact; high-by-default invents a defect. Overall is capped at SOME_CONCERNS wherever a domain is NO_INFORMATION.2

A second, independent assessment was obtained from: gpt-5 Codex (openai family), via `codex exec`3

The assessment above was made by: Claude Opus 5 (anthropic family) -- the assessment above4

How the second assessor was asked: Blind, from scripts/second_assessor_prompt.py, which assembles the prompt from an ALLOW-LIST of registry-sourced factual fields and refuses to send it if any RoB 2 verdict word appears in the assembled text. The second assessor was not shown this assessment and was not asked whether it agreed. It was given this project's NO_INFORMATION-never-LOW rule so the comparison measures judgement rather than house dialect.5

The disagreement rate, reported as disagreement because agreement between two assessors given the same facts authenticates nothing: 2 of 12 judgements -- 16.7%. Reported as disagreement: agreement between two assessors given the same facts authenticates nothing.6

Where they disagree, by domain: D1 2 of 2 disagree, D2 0 of 2 disagree, D3 0 of 2 disagree, D4 0 of 2 disagree, D5 0 of 2 disagree and overall 0 of 2 disagree.7

That rate was measured before this review's D1 judgements moved. It is left as measured: On 2026-08-21 this review's D1 judgements moved from LOW to NO_INFORMATION on the RoB 2 guidance -- the position assessor 2 had taken. The rate above was measured before that and is left exactly as measured: it is a published number, it is the record of what a blind second assessor said, and it is the reason the guidance was re-read. Editing it would delete the evidence that the change was warranted. This is the same computation re-run on the object as it now stands, so both are visible and neither is silently corrected.8

Re-run on the object as it now stands: 0 of 12 judgements -- 0.0%. By domain: D1 0 of 2 disagree, D2 0 of 2 disagree, D3 0 of 2 disagree, D4 0 of 2 disagree, D5 0 of 2 disagree and overall 0 of 2 disagree.9

2 D1 judgement(s) on this topic moved. Any D1 disagreement that remains is one where this assessment said SOME_CONCERNS rather than LOW -- assessor 2 said NO_INFORMATION there too, and the guidance applied here speaks to LOW, not to SOME_CONCERNS. So a claim that 'the D1 disagreement is resolved' would be false wherever those two numbers differ, which is why the count is re-run per topic instead of asserted once.10

D1 now agrees with assessor 2 on every compared result.11

Certainty of the evidence

Certainty was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons..1

No domain is rated UP. Rating up for a large effect, a dose-response gradient or opposing plausible confounding applies to observational evidence; these are randomised trials, which start HIGH and can only be rated down.2

Very LOW certainty. Both contributing results carry unmasked outcome assessment on a partly-judgemental endpoint; the two trials disagree on whether the effect excludes no difference; the pooled quantity is one of two registered primaries; and k = 2 cannot support precision.3

Where a result is rated worse than LOW overall, the domain carrying that judgement is: D4 on 2 result(s), D5 on 2 result(s). The overall rating is the worst domain, so these are the domains that determine it.4

Certainty of the evidence, by outcome, with every rating step5
OutcomeCertaintykStarted atRating steps
therapeutic response (combined clinical and microbiological), test-of-cureVERY_LOW2HIGHrisk of bias -- both results are SOME_CONCERNS and the driver is named: the outcomes assessor is not masked (masking is double -- participant and investigator) on an endpoint whose clinical half is a judgement, and each trial registers two primaries of which this review pools one without recording the choice. D2 and D3 are NO_INFORMATION. (move: HIGH to MODERATE, down 1 level(s)); inconsistency -- The two trials disagree in direction of conclusion: 1.0762 (0.9138 to 1.2676) includes no difference and 1.3426 (1.1334 to 1.5904) excludes it. The stored refit gives I-squared 70.48%, Q 3.3879 on 1 df, p = 0.0657. At k = 2 that I-squared is not itself evidence, but the non-overlap of conclusions is. (move: MODERATE to LOW, down 1 level(s)); indirectness -- The pooled result is one of two registered primary outcomes, chosen without a recorded reason, and the endpoint combines a microbiological result with a clinical judgement. The quantity pooled is therefore not cleanly the quantity a reader would take 'therapeutic response' to mean. (move: LOW to very LOW, down 1 level(s)); imprecision -- k = 2. The Hartung-Knapp interval is RR 1.2007 (0.2946 to 4.8937) on t = 12.7062 with 1 df, and the unadjusted interval crosses no difference. The rating cannot fall below very LOW, so this domain is recorded as warranting a downgrade that the scale cannot express. (move: Very LOW -- already at the floor, no further downgrade applied); publication bias -- k = 2. A funnel plot and its asymmetry tests have essentially no power below about ten trials (Handbook 13.3.5.4), so this is not assessable rather than 'undetected'. (move: Not assessable -- no rating applied)

Discussion

[Draft] The pooled RR is 1.201 (95% CI 0.967 to 1.491) over 2 trials, against nitrofurantoin. Certainty is rated VERY_LOW. Whether a change of that magnitude is clinically meaningful in this population is the author's judgement: no field on this object records a threshold of importance, and none is assumed here.1

[Draft] Across 2 trials, I-squared is 70.5%; tau-squared 0.0172; 1 of the 2 trial intervals include no effect and 1 exclude it. I-squared and tau-squared at k=2 are weak evidence about consistency in either direction. Two points cannot demonstrate agreement, and a low value here means only that the two estimates are consistent with a common effect -- not that one is established. Whether that degree of disagreement matters clinically -- whether the trials are answering the same question in the same patients -- is the author's judgement.2

[Draft] This review pools 1.201 (95% CI 0.967 to 1.491) over 2 trials. The appraised synthesis pooled therapeutic success at test-of-cure, reported as a treatment difference in the pooled micro-ITT population, split by nitrofurantoin susceptibility. Which trials that synthesis carries: Both registration ids are named in the abstract. Read. Why the two results differ -- whether by population, outcome definition, model or included set -- is the author's judgement.3

[Draft] The evidence base is 2 trials, assessed for risk of bias as SOME_CONCERNS on 2 result(s). GRADE certainty is VERY_LOW, rated down for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness and imprecision. Whether that is enough to answer the question depends on the decision the answer is for, which is not stated on this object, and is the author's judgement.4

[Draft] primary trials. No bibliographic search for primary trials was run. The 2 included trials were identified by reading named registrations on 2026-08-18; Both registrations read from ClinicalTrials.gov on 2026-08-18: conditions, arm groups with types, registered primary outcome measures, and the posted results counts and denominators used in the pool. Published syntheses. PubMed E-utilities esearch + esummary, executed 2026-08-21. Query as executed: (gepotidacin[tiab]) and (meta-analysis[pt] OR "systematic review"[pt] OR meta-analysis[tiab] OR "pooled"[tiab] or eagle[tiab]). It matched 25 record(s), of which 25 were retrieved and 25 read; 1 appraised. Whether that is broad enough for the claim this review makes is the author's judgement.5

[Draft] Certainty was rated down for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness and imprecision. What further evidence would change the conclusion is a judgement about a trial nobody has run, and is the author's.6

Comparison with published syntheses

Published syntheses were identified as follows. PubMed E-utilities, executed 2026-08-21. Query, counts and per-record disposition in ssot/gepotidacin-urinary-tract-auto-full-review/appraisal/PUBLISHED_SYNTHESIS_SCREEN.json.1

This review was compared against 1 published synthesis(es); the denominator is stated because a comparison against an unstated number of reviews is not a comparison.2

What this comparison found. The sponsor's own pooled analysis of these exact two trials splits by nitrofurantoin susceptibility, and the effect is more than twice as large in the not-susceptible stratum: therapeutic success difference +9.6% [4.1, 15.2] where the uropathogen is susceptible against +20.8% [9.2, 32.4] where it is not (PMID 42413960, Clin Infect Dis 2026, EAGLE-2 NCT04020341 and EAGLE-3 NCT04187144). This pool collapses that split, so its single ratio is an average over two populations the published analysis keeps apart. They report a risk difference in percentage points and this object pools a risk ratio; theirs is micro-ITT and this object's registered outcome text names no analysis population. Their interval excludes zero and this one includes one, and those are not contradictory statements about one quantity. The pooled analysis is by the sponsor's investigators. That does not make it wrong and it is the most direct evidence about these two trials, but it is stated rather than treated as an independent referee.3

On what basis their trial set is known: Both registration ids are named in the abstract. Read.4

Conclusions

[Draft] Across 2 randomised trials, RR was 1.201 (95% CI 0.967 to 1.491) for therapeutic response (combined clinical and microbiological), test-of-cure visit against nitrofurantoin. Certainty in that estimate is VERY_LOW. That is the estimate. What the evidence shows -- stated as a finding rather than as a number -- is the author's sentence.1
